dedupe_keys.name: bacnet attack dataset for smart building intrusion detection moosavi et al

description: A network traffic dataset for BACnet, the protocol that links HVAC controllers and other devices in smart buildings, built to train and test intrusion detection and prevention systems. Real attack traffic is rarely shared for confidentiality reasons, so the authors, a team from Islamic Azad University Mashhad Branch, took real building data from existing datasets and replayed it as BACnet traffic: a virtual machine per controller ran a controller simulator, and the real readings were injected into the network with their original dates and times. Three attack types were run against this network: falsifying, modifying, and covert channel attacks, the last with the hidden message sent as plain text, hashed with SHA3-256 and encrypted with AES-256. Traffic was captured in pcap format with Wireshark. The article appeared in Data in Brief in 2024 under a CC BY licence; the data availability statement points to a Kaggle BACnet network dataset, and no licence for the data files is stated on the article page. Coverage: a simulated building network, not a live building. Caveats: attacks are synthetic and the baseline traffic is replayed, not recorded from one site. Useful for resilience studies of building control systems and for cyber-attack detection models. It relates to the KARGS BACnet Wireshark captures record in the catalogue.
